The plan in one screen

Three things shape every route

Bangladeshi MBBS (2019–20 session), results out September 2026, internship from Oct–Nov 2026 in Chattogram, no work experience, USD 30k budget. Long-term goal: practise medicine in the US. Fields: public health, epidemiology, global health, clinical research, aerospace medicine.

  1. 1

    Finish the internship

    Without it there is no full BMDC registration, so no FCPS, full GMC, Saudi, Qatar or UAE licence, and no AHPRA registration. Realistic time to leave: December 2027 to April 2028.

  2. 2

    Best bridge to the US

    Take Step 1 during the internship, then a paid US research job, then Step 2 CK, aiming for the 2029 Match. That keeps the graduation recent (about 3 years) and earns US letters of recommendation.

  3. 3

    Apply now, start later

    Erasmus Mundus, Gates Cambridge, KAUST, MEXT, GKS, Stipendium Hungaricum, Türkiye and CSC need no work experience. Most 2027 starts collide with the internship, so ask each programme about late arrival or aim for 2028.

Timeline from now to the 2029 Match

  1. Nov 2026 – Jan 2027 Now

    The application wave

    Funded master's and PhD deadlines cluster here. One master motivation letter, adapted per programme.

  2. Nov 2026 – late 2027

    Internship year

    Unlocks full BMDC registration — the key to every licence route.

  3. 2027

    USMLE Step 1

    Sit it during the internship. Decide on PLAB 1 before Dhaka sittings end in Feb 2027.

  4. Dec 2027 – Apr 2028

    Departure window

    Internship done. Start a funded degree, or a paid research post abroad.

  5. 2028

    US research job + Step 2 CK

    J-1 Research Scholar or H-1B cap-exempt post. US letters. ECFMG Pathway + OET.

  6. March 2029 Goal

    The Match

    Graduation still recent, US experience in hand.

    Full notes & source

    The fastest real exit and the best bridge to a US Match: US letters and recent graduation. Avoid unpaid posts. Visa: J-1 research scholar is safest (ECFMG can sponsor if the host can't). H-1B $100k fee: Proclamation 11069 (18 Sep 2026) extends it to 21 Sep 2027, but a California court vacated the agency policies applying it on 30 Sep (government appealed to the 9th Circuit, 9 Oct) and a Massachusetts ruling also blocks it; appeals pending in the 1st, 9th and D.C. Circuits; as of 15 Oct no court had stayed the rulings (law-firm summaries; dockets not verified). The DHS $103,265 proposal's comment period closed 24 Sep with no final rule. DHS proposed (25 Aug 2026) an extra $103,265 fee for cap-subject petitions only — cap-exempt university employers wouldn't pay it. J-1 'duration of status' rule postponed by a court on 14 Sep. Keep his online presence clean before a J-1 interview. 1 Nov: no new court ruling found; university ISSS guidance (7 Oct) still says the fee is not being collected.

    Official source for Paid US research post (J-1 or H-1B cap-exempt) (opens in a new tab) ↗Verified 1 Nov 2026

    Read the story about USMLE + ECFMG certification →
    Full notes & source

    Step 1 and Step 2 CK plus a Pathway (OET Medicine) are required; with no licence, Pathway 6 (Mini-CEX) is the realistic one. IMGs now apply for USMLE via FSMB (since 12 Jan 2026). Step 2 CK is the score screen. Check the school's ECFMG Sponsor Note on wdoms.org. NRMP 2027 Match: registration opened 15 Sep 2026 (multi-factor login now mandatory), registration deadline 29 Jan 2027, ECFMG requirements due by the rank-list deadline 3 Mar 2027, Match Day 19 Mar 2027 — too early for him; target 2028 or 2029. Policy: the 75-country immigrant-visa pause (Bangladesh included) is no longer in effect since 21 Aug 2026 (court order in CLINIC v. Rubio) — good news for a later green card, but litigation continues. The DHS rule ending J-1 'duration of status' (due 15 Sep 2026) was postponed by a court; ECFMG is watching. As of 1 Nov the only recent ECFMG news post is still the D/S postponement (23 Sep); no 2028 Pathways, OET or fee news. NRMP published three new transition-to-residency data reports on 14 Oct (no rule change). USMLE now uses new software with 30-minute blocks (Step 1: 14 × 30 min since 14 May 2026; Step 2 CK: 16 × 30 min since 7 May 2026) — practise with the new tutorial. Bangladesh is not on the US travel-ban list. NRMP's Oct 2026 Illuminator: programs must give applicants at least 48 hours to answer interview invitations and can't over-invite; a voluntary rank-list lock pilot runs in IM, Pediatrics and Vascular Surgery — no IMG-specific rule change.

    Official source for USMLE + ECFMG certification (opens in a new tab) ↗Verified 1 Nov 2026

    A degree in medicine explicitly qualifies for this program; work experience is 'not required but highly desirable'. The big practical catch is that the GRE is required (unlike Hopkins Epidemiology), with about 3 weeks left. The GRE waiver applies only to people who submitted official GRE scores for the Hopkins MSPH in International Health and were admitted within 10 years; requests were due 1 Nov, so it does not help you. General Bloomberg School rules apply: three letters, WES ICAP or ECE credential evaluation (ECFMG not accepted) and English scores or a WES/ECE-based waiver.     The Interdisciplinary Biomedical Graduate Program is lab-based biomedical science, not public health. Funding is a $41,200 stipend for 2026-27, full tuition remission, individual health insurance and a $2,000 first-year enrichment award. Degree should be in a biological or physical science, mathematics, computer science or engineering, with a minimum GPA of 3.2 of 4 or equivalent (incoming average 3.7); whether an MBBS fits is for the program to judge. All successful applicants have research experience, most with 1+ year in a lab. You need 3 letters (the research-advisor letter is very important) and a personal statement whose research description is heavily weighed; GRE is not required. English: TOEFL iBT 100 (or 5 on the new scale), IELTS 7.0 or Duolingo 120, under 24 months old, unless exempt through a degree from an approved English-instructed institution. Interviews Jan to Mar, overseas by teleconference; offers by 15 April.

    An MBBS is usually accepted for direct entry. JHU Epidemiology: GRE not required, TOEFL ≥100 / IELTS ≥7, 4 years of tuition + stipend. Harvard PHS: fully funded, GRE required for all applicants. UNC: GRE not required; files incomplete on 31 Jan aren't reviewed and department funding isn't guaranteed. By the end he'd be 7–9 years past graduation, which hurts a clinical Match; suits a research career.

    Official source for Funded US PhD (epidemiology, biostatistics, informatics) (opens in a new tab) ↗Verified 17 Oct 2026

    A working route, not a scholarship (personal account by Dr. Iftekhar Ahmed Sakib, not an official source). Applied via SOPHAS to MPH programmes, won scholarship money with no stipend, and covers the rest with US jobs. SOPHAS fee waiver ($155, first programme only) is open to citizens who live in a UN Least Developed Country such as Bangladesh: request it before submitting, then submit within 14 days; an $80 WES coupon is on the same form. F-1: on-campus work 20 hours a week in term (assistantships count), CPT after one full academic year, OPT 12 months. Applying while MBBS or internship is in progress is normal: offers are contingent on completion before enrolment.

Amounts are in each school's own currency. The first SOPHAS programme costs $155 and each extra one $65. Several fees are waivable (Oxford for Bangladesh, SOPHAS on request for Bangladesh as a least-developed country, MBZUAI at 75%+), so treat this as a ceiling.

How to read it. 0 means no funded route exists. 1–2 is a long shot: elite schemes with a few dozen awards, usually won by people with research records. 3 is an outside chance worth a strong application. Open any route for the four-factor breakdown and what would raise the score.

The pattern. No scholarship or PhD scores above 4. The best odds among scholarships are the government schemes where Bangladesh is a partner (such as Stipendium Hungaricum, on the Europe site) and the health-focused Erasmus Mundus programmes. The higher scores (up to 6) belong to steps you largely control, such as ECFMG certification, PLAB and US observerships, where the score measures whether you can complete the step, not a competition. The biggest levers are the same everywhere: a class-rank certificate, one research output during the internship, and applying to intakes you can actually start (January 2028 or later).

All four main deadlines are Tuesday 1 December 2026, US Eastern. Official pages arbitrate; items below marked 'not found' were not stated on the official pages read.

Hopkins Bloomberg PhD Epidemiology (SOPHAS)
  • Deadline: submit by 1 Dec 2026; supporting documents (letters, transcripts, evaluation) no later than two weeks after the deadline (official rule). Cycle opened 12 Aug 2026.
  • Fee: $155 first programme, $65 each additional. International waiver exists but must be requested before you submit; once approved you have 14 days to submit and it covers the first $155 only.
  • Letters: 3 required (Epi FAQ: at least one academic, an advisor preferred; may mix academic and professional). Trap: SOPHAS can show the file complete with 2, but Bloomberg still requires the third.
  • Statement: statement of objectives and research goals. The Epi FAQ states a two-page limit (earlier notes said none; corrected). The generic how-to-apply page gives no limit. CV/resume required. No adviser needed in advance; faculty may be named.
  • Credential evaluation is mandatory for international coursework: WES ICAP course-by-course through SOPHAS, or ECE course-by-course sent to Bloomberg. ECFMG certification is not accepted. WES ICAP costs $239 (the $80 coupon applies if the SOPHAS waiver is approved), plus delivery fees. WES's clock starts only when documents are accepted; the evaluation then takes about 1-2 weeks; door to door 4-6 weeks.
  • English (scores under 2 years old): TOEFL iBT 100 for scores before 21 Jan 2026; 5.0 on the new 1-6 scale for scores after 21 Jan 2026 (a test taken now uses the new scale); IELTS Academic 7; Duolingo 130; PTE 68. Waiver only if a WES or ECE evaluation verifies English as the sole language of instruction for the bachelor's/professional degree; the waiver cannot apply until the evaluation is received. Medium-of-instruction letters are not accepted. Duolingo/PTE scores go directly to BSPH Admissions Services.
  • Work experience (conflict inside JHU): the programme page lists one year of full-time work in a related field as required; the Epi FAQ calls one year of full-time post-baccalaureate work only 'strongly recommended' for ScM and PhD. Whether the internship year counts is not stated. Email BSPH.EpiAcademic@jh.edu.
  • GRE: not required and not reviewed.
  • Submit-early caveat: SOPHAS lets you submit before transcripts and recommendations arrive, but it will not review or verify the application until all transcripts, payments and recommendations are received. Allow up to 10 business days of SOPHAS verification.
Emory Rollins PhD Epidemiology (LaneyConnect)
  • Deadline: final deadline 1 Dec 2026 (deadlines fall at midnight US Eastern). Fee: $75 (waivers exist per notes).
  • Letters: 3, from people familiar with your academic performance.
  • Statement of purpose, 500 words: previous research experience or training, research interests, how the programme addresses them, long-term goals. Plus the Statement on Building Collaborative and Respectful Graduate Communities (500 words) and an optional diversity statement.
  • Name at least two Epidemiology graduate faculty you want to work with. CV/resume required.
  • Transcripts: upload scanned registrar-issued transcripts (web printouts not accepted); non-English transcripts need notarized translation. Official transcripts only after admission.
  • Credential evaluation (conflict, ask): the programme and Laney pages do not make it mandatory (Laney: international applicants 'may want to consider' one). But the general Rollins how-to-apply page says international applicants must use WES, and that page covers all degrees including the SOPHAS MPH. Ask Epi admissions before relying on 'no WES'.
  • English: TOEFL/IELTS for international applicants; no numeric Epidemiology minimum found (do not borrow another programme's number). Contact the programme about the English-medium waiver.
  • Stipend: $43,260 for FY26-27 per Laney (CBA rate); the Rollins programme page still shows the stale $42,000 (2025-26). Full tuition scholarship per the Rollins page. GRE optional.
  • Odds and next steps: about 200+ applications for 10-14 places; a virtual visit day is usually a Friday in the first two weeks of February.
Pittsburgh IBGP PhD (lab-based biomedical science)
  • Deadline: Fall 2027 application open 1 Sep to 1 Dec 2026 (no time of day stated); review is rolling and early files help. Fee: $50, non-refundable, due before processing; a need-based waiver was not found on the pages read (ask).
  • Letters: minimum 3; the FAQ says the research-advisor letter is very important.
  • Personal statement: required; no word limit or prompt on the pages read; the research description is heavily weighed. CV: not listed as a requirement (upload one if the portal allows). Transcripts are uploaded in the application; no WES requirement stated.
  • English: TOEFL iBT 100 (or 5 on the new scoring), IELTS 7.0, Duolingo 120; scores under 24 months old on 1 Sep of the start term. Exempt only with a bachelor's or higher from a US regionally accredited or other approved English-instructed institution ('approved' is not defined) - plan on needing a real score. TOEFL institution code 2927, dept 45.
  • Academic bar: minimum GPA 3.2 on 4.0 (incoming average 3.7); GRE not required. The degree is expected to be in a biological or physical science, mathematics, computer science or engineering; whether an MBBS fits is for the programme to judge.
  • Honest weak point: all successful applicants have research experience, most at least a year in a lab. A clinician's manuscript portfolio is the counter-argument; front-load it in the statement.
  • Timeline: interviews mostly January to March (overseas by teleconference); acceptances rolling 1 Feb to 15 Apr; offer letters mailed before 15 April.
Yale School of Public Health PhD (via the Graduate School, GSAS)
  • Deadline: 1 Dec 2026, 11:59 pm Eastern (deadlines are subject to change). The public health PhD must use the GSAS PhD/Master's application, not SOPHAS. Fall 2027 application is open at apply.grad.yale.edu/apply. Contact: phdms.publichealth@yale.edu.
  • Departments: Biostatistics, Chronic Disease Epidemiology, Environmental Health Sciences, Epidemiology of Microbial Diseases, Social and Behavioral Sciences, Health Policy and Management.
  • Fee: $105; US citizens, permanent residents and non-US citizens can all request a waiver.
  • Funding: all PhD students are guaranteed five years of 12-month stipend and tuition support (fellowships, teaching fellowships, traineeships, research assistantships) plus health coverage. GSAS tuition 2026-27 is $52,400 and is covered. GSAS 2026-27 minimum stipends: $52,046 (humanities/social/physical sciences) and $53,629 (biological and biomedical); the Public Health band was not stated. A $1,500 one-time relocation award is confirmed.
  • Letters: 3, entered by name in the application; letters need not arrive before submission, but review starts shortly after the deadline. CV required; no writing sample.
  • Statement of academic purpose: research interests and faculty; you may list up to three faculty; no mentor needed in advance. The YSPH page states no word limit; the 500-1,000 word figure in earlier notes was not found (check the GSAS Application Question FAQs).
  • GRE: required only for Biostatistics (PhD and MS) and Health Policy and Management (PhD); not accepted for the other four PhD departments; no waivers; self-report scores; institution code 3987.
  • English (PhD): the PhD page gives only Speaking minimums (to teach): TOEFL iBT Speaking 26+ (before 21 Jan 2026) or 5.5+ (on or after); IELTS 'speaking 8.0 or higher' as written. The 100 / 7.0 overall figures are the MS minimum, not the PhD. Average admitted PhD: TOEFL 106, IELTS 7.5. Duolingo not accepted. Waiver: undergraduate degree from a school where English is the primary language of instruction with at least three years in residence; no waiver based on an advanced degree.
  • Transcripts: unofficial transcripts uploaded with the application; records in English or translated; no WES requirement seen (but no explicit 'no WES' statement either).
  • Eligibility and odds: a master's is not required (some programmes prefer post-baccalaureate training); whether an MBBS counts as the bachelor's equivalent is not ruled on - email the programme. 5-year average acceptance 3% across the six departments; average admitted GPA 3.8, no minimum. Decisions mostly February to early March; reply by 15 April.
Hopkins GDEC PhD and Columbia MPH (optional add-ons)
  • Hopkins PhD in Global Disease Epidemiology and Control (found by Claude on 9 Nov, not in your notes; read on publichealth.jhu.edu): the page says the prior graduate degree can be "a degree in medicine, veterinary medicine, or dentistry", so an MBBS qualifies on its face. Prior work experience is "not required but highly desirable" (the Epi PhD asks for a year). Apply by 1 December for an August start. The catch: standardized test scores (GRE) are required, and the department waives this only for people who already submitted official GRE scores to Hopkins' MSPH in International Health within the last 10 years. Hopkins says it reviews applications holistically. It is STEM designated (24-month OPT extension). Same BSPH PhD stipend guarantee as the Epi PhD ($52,000 minimum through June 2027, tuition, fees, medical benefits). Not checked: letters and statement rules for this programme, GRE seat availability and score-delivery time before 1 Dec. Run it through SOPHAS (one more designated programme, $65 extra if added to the Hopkins Epi application).
  • Columbia Mailman MPH: preferred deadline 1 Dec 2026 (priority review and full scholarship consideration); standard deadline 15 Jan 2027 (rolling); 1 Mar 2027 late consideration (reviewed as space remains, scholarships subject to availability). Applies via SOPHAS; Statement of Purpose max 500 words.
  • Columbia money: merit awards $7,500-$30,000 per year; need-based grants ($10,000-$12,500) are FAFSA-based, so assume none for an international applicant; the 'PopFam $10,000' figure from earlier notes was not checked. Partial funding only (the Sakib model), not a funded PhD.
The letters
  • Count: 3 strong letters + 1 backup referee cover all of Hopkins, Emory, Pittsburgh and Yale; the same referees serve all of them and each portal sends its own request link. MRC (27 Nov) needs 2 referees with institutional email addresses, so brief the same people about both sets of dates.
  • Who: (1) research supervisor or senior co-author (the Pittsburgh 'research advisor' slot and the most important letter everywhere); (2) a professor who taught or examined you and can rank you against other students; (3) a clinical or internship supervisor or senior collaborator; (4) a backup senior name asked at the same time.
  • Briefing pack for each referee: CV draft, SOP draft (even rough), transcript, one line on each programme, exact deadlines, and 4-5 specific things they personally saw you do (a dataset cleaned, an analysis run, a deadline saved). Generic letters are the known failure mode.
  • Statements: Hopkins research-weighted within two pages; Emory a hard 500 words naming 2 faculty; Pittsburgh research description first; Yale research interests plus up to 3 faculty.

1 Dec in Baltimore, Atlanta, Pittsburgh and New Haven runs to about the next morning in Dhaka; do not plan on that buffer.

Honest timing note and open gates
  • A fully verified SOPHAS file by 1 Dec is not achievable from a standing start in November (WES approval plus up to 10 business days of SOPHAS verification). What is achievable, and normal, is a complete submitted file with WES verification following within the two-week supporting-document window.
  • The risk sits with Hopkins' WES-dependent English waiver: a real test score, if you can book one, de-risks the whole round.
  • Open gates to resolve by email this week: Hopkins work-experience line; Emory WES (ask); whether an MBBS counts as the bachelor's equivalent at Yale; Pittsburgh fee waiver and MBBS fit.
  • Hopkins SOPHAS fee waiver (pack notes, not re-verified): Epidemiology is not among the departments with its own waiver.

MRC North West PhD, 27 November 2026

A fully funded four-year biomedical PhD at Manchester and Liverpool, open to international applicants, closing Friday 27 November 2026 and applied for through up to two named projects. This pack lists what the official pages confirm, what is still unconfirmed (MBBS eligibility, fee) and a supervisor-first timeline.

  • Manchester + Liverpool
  • PhD, 4 years
  • UKRI stipend
  • Project-led

Closes27 Nov 2026in 24 days

At a glance

DeadlineFriday 27 November 2026 (no closing time of day stated on the page); projects and applications opened 30 Oct 2026

The MRC file is project-led, not portal-led: you apply to a named advertised project (up to two, each a separate application), and contacting the supervisor first is described as one of the most important steps before applying.

What the application requires (official pages, re-verified)
  • Eligibility: First or Upper Second-class UK honours degree (or international equivalent) in a relevant discipline, held or about to be obtained. A master's is not required, but many successful applicants have one or research experience. Whether an MBBS with the internship still in progress counts is not stated; ask the Doctoral Academy.
  • Two projects maximum: each is a separate application with its own tailored supporting statement. Main supervisor only is entered in the portal.
  • Documents: supporting statement; reference details; degree certificates and final or interim transcripts; official English certificates if applicable; CV is required. The page states: 'A research statement is not required for this programme.'
  • Supporting statement: no specific word limit; 2-4 pages maximum recommended (FBMH general page; earlier notes said 1-2 pages).
  • References: two references from people who know your academic ability; one may be from your clinical or work background; the referee email must be institutional, not personal. Referees receive an automatic request when you submit, and you cannot be nominated without references. (This is the FBMH general research-degree page; confirm in the portal.)
  • English: not required at the point of application; any offer is conditional on an approved English test (such as IELTS). FBMH general guidance: typically IELTS 6.5 overall (5.5 each component, 6.0 writing) or TOEFL iBT 90; some programmes 7.0. Tests are valid 2 years; ask whether an English-medium MBBS qualifies for a waiver.
  • Application fee: not found on the programme page; confirm in the portal before assuming no fee.
  • Portal entry values (use exactly): Level Postgraduate Research; Entry year 2027/28; Intake September (although the studentship starts October 2027); Funding: Research Council / MRC PhD Studentship / Awarded / Fully Funded.
  • No WES or credential evaluation requirement stated for this programme; do not order WES for Manchester. No GRE requirement stated.
Fit note and project shortlist
  • Fit: this is a biomedical-science DTP and most advertised projects are lab-based. Your fit is decided by project choice, not programme title: population, clinical-data, modelling and prescribing projects are where an MBBS plus your manuscript portfolio is a strength; a wet-lab molecular project would be a weak file.
  • Titles below came from FindAPhD listings on 7 Nov, not the official projects list; confirm each on Manchester's official projects page (supervisor emails and prerequisites live there) before emailing.
  • 1. Rebuilding trust in vaccination: a Large Epidemic Model to predict immunity gaps (Liverpool; Dr S Chen, Prof A J Jorgensen): best fit; your dengue and cold-mortality trend work and GBD experience map onto it.
  • 2. Closing the loop: AI-guided approach to prioritise competence experimentation of emerging arbovirus risk (Liverpool): strong fit with your dengue work.
  • 3. Genomic and mathematical approaches for precise targeting of public health interventions to control viral emergence (Precision Medicine DLA): strong fit.
  • 4. Antibiotic use in hidradenitis suppurativa: prescribing patterns, treatment trajectories and antimicrobial treatment failure (Manchester): good fit, clinical and data-led.
  • 5. Personalised approaches to reduce indoor environmental exposures during pregnancy (Manchester): good fit, exposure epidemiology.
  • 6. A digital portal incorporating PROMs for equity and effectiveness of outpatient epilepsy care: good fit, health services and equity.
  • 7. Optimising data completeness in clinical prediction models with high-frequency patient-generated health data (Manchester): good fit; your NHANES/GBD data work is the argument.
  • 8. Reliable Multimodal Agentic AI for cardiovascular disease diagnosis and risk prediction (Manchester): adjacent fit; heavy AI-methods weight.
  • Suggested pairing: (1) + (2), both Liverpool public-health modelling; or (1) + (4) for a Liverpool and Manchester spread. Do not pair two lab-heavy projects.
Supervisor email template (send Mon 9 - Tue 10 Nov)

Subject: Prospective MRC NW-DMS applicant: [exact project title]. Body 150-200 words with your academic CV attached.

Content: who you are (Bangladeshi MBBS graduate, internship, Chattogram); one line naming a specific paper or project of theirs and why it matters; two lines on you (degree, one relevant skill, one result with numbers such as a submitted manuscript or dataset analysed); the connection to their project and one question showing you read it; the ask (a brief call, and is an MBBS applicant without a prior master's a realistic fit?). Close with the 27 Nov deadline.

One polite reminder after a week with no reply, then move on; a generic mass email is spotted and ignored.

Still to confirm (do not state as fact)
  • Does an MBBS with the internship in progress meet the degree requirement? (Ask admissions.)
  • Application fee: not found.
  • Exact per-project document list and referee count inside the portal (the step-by-step section did not render in a plain fetch).
  • Whether the 2027/28 stipend rate is above GBP 21,805.
  • Whether your English-medium MBBS gets a waiver from the offer-stage test.

One enquiry email to fbmh.doctoralacademy.admissions@manchester.ac.uk can settle MBBS eligibility, English waiver and fee in a single ask.

Guide

SOPHAS: fees, waiver, costs and applying mid-internship

SOPHAS charges $155 for the first programme and $65 for each additional one, and Bangladesh qualifies for the international waiver if you request it before submitting. You can apply during the internship, but SOPHAS will not review the file until transcripts, payments and letters arrive.

  • $155 / $65
  • Fee waiver
  • WES $239
  • Mid-internship
Fees and the international waiver
  • Fees: $155 for the first programme and $65 for each additional (SOPHAS Applicant Help Center, updated 6 Aug 2026). Some programmes add a supplemental fee.
  • Fund is limited: waivers are first-come, first-served and 'can be quickly depleted'. There is no public counter; call SOPHAS customer service on 617-612-2090 before requesting. You need an account; requests by mail or email are not accepted.
  • Bangladesh qualifies: you must be a citizen of and currently reside in a country on the UN Least Developed Countries list; Bangladesh is on SOPHAS's own list.
  • Covers the first designation only ($155); each additional programme's $65 is still payable. One waiver type per cycle.
  • $80 WES coupon: the form also lets you request $80 off a WES course-by-course evaluation; valid for your initial WES order only, no refunds once the order is placed. WES ICAP itself costs $239 (course-by-course Basic is $186, but Hopkins requires ICAP).
  • Must request before submitting. Requests after submission are not honoured. Processing takes up to 10 business days and you cannot submit while the request is pending.
  • 14-day clock: once approved you must submit within 14 days including weekends and holidays; no extensions; missing it voids the waiver and you cannot reapply. Outstanding transcripts, recommendations and scores need not arrive within the 14 days.
Sequencing the waiver against the deadlines
  • Because approval can take up to 10 business days and then starts a 14-day clock, request it only when the application is essentially ready to submit, but not so late that processing eats the deadline: for a 1 Dec Hopkins deadline, a request around Tue 10 - Wed 11 Nov leaves room.
  • If the waiver has not been approved by about Fri 20 Nov, weigh simply paying $155 to protect the deadline.
  • The waiver covers one programme: use it on the most expensive-to-miss first designation and pay the $65 extras.
Applying mid-internship
  • Yes, you can apply in the final phase of the degree. Universities require the degree completed by enrolment, not by the application date; none of the four MPH programmes checked requires work experience or internship completion for admission.
  • SOPHAS mechanics: in-progress and planned coursework is a normal part of the application. You can submit before transcripts and recommendations are received, but SOPHAS will not review or verify the application until all transcripts, payments and recommendations arrive.
  • Emory (official FAQ): applicants near completion may apply in their final year with incomplete transcripts; an offer is contingent on a final transcript documenting completion.
  • Drexel: 'The MPH programs do not require work experience' confirmed. The exact 'prior to enrolling' wording was not seen on the page read; it asks for a bachelor's or equivalent international degree.
  • Georgia State: 'bachelor's at the time of enrollment' was not verified (catalog page fetch failed). UIC: bachelor's in any field, GPA typically 3.00, GRE not required; 'in progress' wording not found.
  • Academic Update (2026-27 cycle): 21 Jun - 30 Jul 2027, updated transcripts by 5 Aug 2027, but it is written for US and English-Canadian coursework; for a Bangladeshi MBBS the practical update route is an updated evaluation or transcript per programme instructions, so confirm with each programme.
  • Cycle dates: opened 12 Aug 2026; closes 2 Aug 2027, 11:59 PM ET; transcripts and test scores matched by 5 Aug 2027, 5 PM ET. Individual programme deadlines are much earlier.
  • MBBS conferral is a matriculation question, not an eligibility one: the degree must be finished by the time the programme starts.

Where the realistic chances are
  • Admission: MPH cohorts routinely include physicians; the screens are the degree, GPA conversion, English scores and the statement. None of the 12 lists research experience as an admission requirement. The public universities (Georgia State, UIC, USF, UAB, Albany) plus Drexel and Tulane are the realistic-admission band; Emory, Columbia, BU, GW and Brown are competitive for everyone and their top merit tiers are the long shots.
  • Where Sakib-type mechanics exist: assistantships with tuition waiver (Georgia State confirmed; UIC unconfirmed), Emory REAL (up to $3,000/semester), Drexel's research fellowship (tuition scholarship + RA), and automatic merit review at stated priority dates (Emory, Drexel, GW, UIC, Albany). USF is the counterexample: it tells internationals to arrive self-funded.
  • None passes the board's hard filter (full tuition + stipend guaranteed). Every route is partial scholarship plus work, and first-year funds must be documentable for the I-20 regardless of expected earnings.
  • Sakib's own case (7 Nov talk, unverified claim): a 50% Columbia scholarship still left a very large balance; he calls the MPH a 'cash-in' programme.
  • Research experience matters mainly for the top merit money and for landing RA jobs after arrival, not for admission itself.
Fee waiver sequencing
  • One SOPHAS account, one transcript and WES set reused across programmes; each added programme costs $65 (UIC adds an $80 supplement, USF a separate application).
  • The international fee waiver (Bangladesh is on the UN LDC list on SOPHAS's page) covers only the first $155 and must be requested before submitting; approval takes up to 10 business days, then you must submit within 14 days or lose it for good.
  • Request it when WES is ordered and the statement is near final. Make the earliest-deadline programme your first designation.
  • Also use the waiver form to claim the $80 WES coupon before placing the WES order (initial order only).
F-1 work rules (official wording)
  • On campus: no more than 20 hours a week while school is in session; full-time during scheduled breaks. You may apply up to 30 days before classes start. RA/TA/GA assistantships count as on-campus employment inside the same cap.
  • CPT: needs at least a full academic year of full-time enrolment (exception for programmes whose curriculum requires earlier training); must be integral to the curriculum; one employer per authorisation. One year of full-time CPT eliminates OPT eligibility.
  • OPT: 12 months per level of study, authorised by USCIS with an EAD; STEM extension (24 months) only for eligible STEM degrees.
  • Off-campus work otherwise needs one full academic year plus economic hardship. Do not plan year-1 income around off-campus work.

Third-party guidance

What other applicants say: guidance posts and the Sakib talk

Summaries of social-media guidance posts and the 7 November BOB-MedElites talk by Dr Sakib, plus the status of every lead they raised. These are personal views, not official rules; the unnamed Netherlands award is now identified as the University of Twente Scholarship.

  • Unofficial
  • Sakib talk
  • Lead status
Building an extracurricular (ECA) profile from home (Career & Abroad, Facebook reel (Bangla), 28 Oct 2026)
  • The reel is about building an extracurricular-activity (ECA) profile from home, and the title promises 15 free resources.
  • No scholarship, programme, amount or deadline is named anywhere in the caption.
  • The list of 15 resources was not retrieved (Facebook gave no captions for this reel), so only the title and caption are known.
  • How to use it: watch the reel yourself and note the 15 items, then keep only those that fit your health, research or public-health field.

Caution: Only the title and caption were read; the actual 15 resources were not retrieved, so nothing here is confirmed content of the reel.

How to make a Europass CV for higher studies (Mrinmoy 'Moon' Modak (Graduate Research Assistant, University of Florida), Nextop USA Facebook group, long Bangla post, 1 Nov 2026)
  • Europass is the EU's free online CV builder; build it only on the official site, europass.europa.eu/en/create-europass-cv. You can make an account or use a guest option, then download a PDF.
  • It is not mandatory everywhere. If a university or scholarship gives its own CV format, use that. USA, Canada, Australia and UK programmes often prefer their own 2 to 3 page academic CV.
  • Order of sections: basic info (professional email, LinkedIn or research profile), Education (latest degree first, official degree names, CGPA if relevant, thesis title), Work experience, Research experience or projects, Publications and presentations, Skills, Languages, Awards, References.
  • For research roles, write what you did, how, and your own role: project title, lab or institution, supervisor, duration, objectives, your contribution, methods, analysis tools.
  • List publications with authors, year, title, journal, DOI and an honest status (Published, Accepted, Under review, Submitted). Never show an unpublished manuscript as published.
  • Name only skills and software you really know (R, Python, SPSS, Excel, GIS and so on). IELTS or TOEFL: give test name, score and date if relevant.
  • Ask referees before you put their names in; leave references out if none are asked for.
  • For a PhD, stress education, research experience, publications, research skills, conference presentations and research interests so a professor sees the match with their work.
  • Keep a folder system (Academic Documents, Transcripts, CV, Research Experience, Publications, IELTS/TOEFL, Recommendation Letters, Awards, SOP and Research Proposal) and one master CV, then make a trimmed version per programme.
  • Before sending, check spelling, degree names, dates, CGPA, email, phone and formatting, and save as YourName_Academic_CV.pdf.

Caution: The post is general advice by a PhD-stage student, not an official rule; always follow each university's own CV instructions. The author promises a follow-up on emailing professors.

Month-by-month application calendar for the Sept 2027 intake (Deshi Passport, Facebook reel with full post text (Bangla), 21 Oct 2026)
  • Oct to Dec (start now): Sweden 16 Oct 2026 to 15 Jan 2027; Norway around 1 Dec; Stipendium Hungaricum expected to open in November (no official date yet); ETH Zurich and EPFL masters usually Nov to Dec (sources differ, check the university site); Charles University English medicine 30 Nov; Greece English masters Dec to May, many 31 May; Netherlands: Studielink applications open from October.
  • January: Finland 7 to 21 Jan 2027 (Studyinfo.fi); Sweden closes 15 Jan; Hungary likely mid-January (last year 15 Jan); Germany summer semester usually 15 Jan; Radboud with scholarship 31 Jan; Comenius University Slovakia 31 Jan to 31 Mar; most Erasmus Mundus deadlines Dec to Jan.
  • Feb to Mar: WU Vienna English masters 1 Feb to 31 Mar; Denmark masters until 1 Mar (DTU 15 Jan to 1 Mar); Italy usually Feb to Apr by university; Charles University 28 Feb to 30 Apr; KU Leuven and Ghent from 1 Mar; Vilnius 1 Mar to 30 Jun; Campus France Feb to Mar.
  • Apr to May: Netherlands without scholarship usually 1 Apr (Radboud basis), some programmes 1 May; Tartu and Tallinn 1 Apr; Latvia RSU 1 Apr to 30 Jun; Portugal Mar to Jul (apply by May to leave visa time); KU Leuven until 15 May; Greece 31 May.
  • Jun to Jul: Spain public universities May to Jul (Complutense and Barcelona 31 Jul); Germany winter semester usually 15 Jul, many earlier; Lithuania 30 Jun; Latvia 30 Jun or 31 Jul; Portugal 31 Jul. Poland has no single date; each university sets its own.
  • Start APS, transcripts, certificate verification and IELTS 3 to 6 months early; a late deadline is not a reason to start late.
  • Visa processing takes long, especially for Germany, so leave time after an offer.
  • The poster's own rule: dates change yearly, so check each one on the university or official portal before you apply.

Caution: This is one creator's compiled calendar; the poster says dates shift each year, and the Swiss dates and the Hungary opening date are flagged uncertain in the post itself. Verify each date on the official portal.

The bank-statement mistake that gets Italy study visas rejected (Imran Faruk Official (education consultant), Facebook reel (Bangla), 22 Feb 2026)
  • The commonest mistake is fake transactions: withdrawing and re-depositing the same money again and again (for example cycling Tk 5 lakh) so the statement looks long and busy.
  • The pattern the speaker warns about: keep Tk 2 to 5 lakh rolling, then deposit the real Tk 20 to 25 lakh only in the last 2 to 3 months before submitting.
  • Why it fails, he says: the balance never really grows, and turnover does not match the sponsor's salary. Example: salary Tk 1.5 lakh a month with half spent means the highest normal transaction is about Tk 2 to 2.5 lakh, not Tk 10 to 15 lakh a month.
  • A visa officer who sees this may reject you for dishonesty.
  • What to do instead: let the account follow real life. Pay school fees, medical bills, shopping, restaurant bills, mobile recharge, bKash transfers and family support through the bank or card, and withdraw small amounts instead of one big monthly cash withdrawal.
  • When 12 months of statements match your real spending and your supporting documents, the embassy is more likely to believe the whole file.

Caution: This is a consultant's own view of how Italian visa officers read statements, not an embassy rule; check the embassy and university pages for the actual financial requirements.

Skills that put you ahead for a fully funded Public Health scholarship (Dhrubo (ধ্রুব), Facebook text post (Bangla), 1 Nov 2026)
  • For applicants with good results but no research experience or publications: learn technical skills now so you can show professors a usable skill set.
  • Statistics software or language: R, Stata, SPSS, Python or SAS. You do not need all; start with one and add others by work type.
  • Epidemiology and biostatistics methods: logistic regression, linear regression, survival analysis, Cox regression, meta-analysis, systematic review, sample-size calculation. Learn the ones that fit your research interest.
  • Research tools: REDCap, Rayyan, RevMan, Zotero, NVivo. Start with Zotero; add Rayyan and RevMan for systematic review or meta-analysis.
  • GIS and disease mapping: QGIS or ArcGIS; start with QGIS.
  • Aim: a stronger profile for funded graduate programmes and a clearer skills story when you write to professors.

Caution: General advice from a social-media post; it names no scheme, amount or deadline and does not promise funding.

Can you get full funding with no research experience? (Toma Rahman, Facebook reel (Bangla and English, about 2 min), 2 Nov 2026)
  • Her answer: saying you cannot get funding without research experience would be a lie, but she has seen people get funded with little; those are exceptions, and most funded research masters and PhD students have some research experience, strong or weak.
  • Her own case: no undergraduate thesis at Dhaka University, but she worked as a research assistant from first year.
  • She also helped others with theses: data collection, interview transcripts, data management, literature review. She had not run her own full research.
  • In her application she said plainly that she had not written a thesis but had done these tasks, and wanted to learn through the thesis. She says it worked.
  • Her advice: try your best to get at least some research experience.
  • If your university cannot offer it, she says it may not be the right university for you, which she calls a harsh comment.

Caution: One person's experience and opinion, with no scheme named; her story shows it can work, not that it will.

The '50+ scholarship opportunities' list post (Bashar Gulumbe, Facebook text post, 2 Nov 2026)
  • The post says the author compiled 50+ scholarships and funded research programmes with deadlines from November 2026 into 2027.
  • The list itself is in the comments or links, and it was not retrieved; the post body names no scheme, amount or deadline.
  • Do not use the count of 50+ as a source.
  • If you open the list, check every scheme on its own official site before spending time or money (the same tip as in Naim's Diary, see the government-scholarship entry).

Caution: Aggregator teaser; nothing in it was checked, and the actual list was never seen.

Four student profiles with the best Italy study-visa chances (Imran Faruk Official (consultant, ends with a client pitch), Facebook reel (Bangla, auto-captions), 13 Oct 2026)
  • Profile 1, bachelor's applicants: HSC GPA 4.0 or more out of 5 (or diploma CGPA 3.0 or more out of 4), IELTS 6.0 or more, and an entrance or CEnT-S exam pass; show about Tk 30 to 40 lakh with genuine transactions and proper sponsor papers. Two factors matter most: the entrance exam and bank solvency.
  • Profile 2, fresh graduates (within about 1 to 3 years): CGPA 3.3 or more out of 4, even with no job; IELTS 6.0 or more (applying on MOI alone lowers the odds); show about Tk 25 to 35 lakh of genuine sponsor funds, consistent with the sponsor's documents.
  • Profile 3, graduated about 3 to 5 years ago: a decent CGPA, 1 to 2 years of job experience related to the degree, IELTS 6.0 or more, Tk 25 to 35 lakh or more, and a perfect sponsor file. The figures in this stretch were garbled in the captions, so treat them as approximate.
  • Profile 4, graduated about 5 to 10 years ago: a moderate CGPA is fine (about 3.0 or 3.5), with 2 to 5 years of job experience, best at a multinational or reputed company and in the same field. He says some get visas on MOI, but IELTS makes it risk-free. These applicants fund themselves partly from savings and rely less on a sponsor. Figures here are also approximate.
  • For every profile the bank statement and the sponsor's financial papers must be consistent and genuine.
  • He says these are his own observations from several years of casework, not a rule, and that other profiles can also get visas.

Caution: Consultant marketing; the lakh figures and CGPA and IELTS cut-offs are one agent's experience, not Italian embassy requirements, and some figures were garbled in the captions. Check the embassy page.

How to get a government scholarship: the full process (Naim's Diary, long Facebook video (Bangla), 1 Nov 2026)
  • Step 1, analyse your results honestly. For bachelor's applicants he says most government scholarships need HSC GPA 4.5 or more out of 5 (5.0 best). For master's applicants, CGPA above 3.0; a 2.8 or 2.9 can sometimes be covered by strong extracurriculars, which HSC applicants cannot do.
  • Lower-competition schemes exist (he gives an ICCR-type scholarship as an example, around 3.8 to 4.0) but with limited subjects.
  • Step 2, organise documents. Use a real scanner, not phone photos, with a clear folder structure. Basics: passport, passport photo, NID, birth certificate, academic documents, extracurricular proof, language certificate if any; sometimes police clearance and a medical certificate.
  • Step 3, build an Excel sheet of target schemes: name, documents needed, when the circular comes, deadline, whether IELTS or police clearance is needed, and the application link.
  • Examples he names: Chinese government, Stipendium Hungaricum, Russian, Kazakhstan, ICCR, Morocco, Mexican and Romanian government scholarships.
  • Where to find them: the Bangladesh ministry site he names as shade.gov.bd (as heard in the transcript, spelling unconfirmed) for ministry-routed offers, and opportunitiescorner.com for international ones. Then go to each scheme's own site for details, to avoid scams and mistakes.
  • Step 4, apply: register, fill the form exactly as instructed, upload documents. A few schemes add an entrance exam or interview (he cites the Russian one); most do not.

Caution: Aimed mainly at HSC and bachelor's applicants, so the GPA cut-offs are the speaker's rules of thumb and mostly not your level; the website names are as transcribed and should be checked.

What to do to win an undergraduate scholarship (Annels Scarlen Diaz, Nextop USA group, Facebook photo post (Bangla), 3 Nov 2026)
  • Aimed at HSC-level students, so it is not your level; the ideas below are what the post says.
  • Keep SSC and HSC results strong and consistent; add subject depth through Olympiads, science fairs and projects.
  • Prepare IELTS or TOEFL, and for the US the SAT only where required (many universities are test-optional; check each one).
  • Choose a few extracurriculars and stay long enough to show real impact rather than collecting 20 certificates.
  • Show leadership by starting small initiatives: free tutoring, a reading or science club, a clean-up or tree planting. Document what you did, why, and what changed.
  • Tailor profile, story and essays to each university; do not copy others' essays or exaggerate.
  • Build relationships with teachers early so recommenders can write real examples.
  • Research who gives financial aid to international students: full tuition or tuition plus living, separate application, SAT or ACT, deadlines, family financial papers. In the USA need-based aid and merit scholarships are different things.
  • Keep an Excel plan with a reach, match and safer list, and prepare essays, letters and financial papers well before deadlines.

Caution: Undergraduate-level advice; an attached table comparing countries was partly illegible and its figures were not used.

Studying in the USA with zero living cost: the Resident Assistant route (Mohammed Farhan Hossain (Bangladeshi undergraduate in Massachusetts), Facebook reel (Bangla and English), 28 Dec 2025)
  • He arrived on a merit scholarship that covered tuition only in part and not living costs, which were roughly double his tuition share.
  • On seniors' advice he applied for a Resident Assistant (RA) post in his residence hall: a free single room, a meal plan and a biweekly stipend, so living cost is effectively $0.
  • Apply as early as the application opens. The pipeline is application, selection, interview, then a training class, taking one to two semesters.
  • Look for three on-campus roles first: Resident Assistant, Research Assistant (approach professors directly, before or right after arriving, saying what skills you bring), and Teaching Assistant.
  • Search on Handshake; build a detailed profile with a professional photo and apply early and widely.
  • F-1 student visa limit: 20 working hours a week; do not exceed it, because employers can report it.
  • His view: use the degree years for long-term growth and skills rather than cash work off campus.

Caution: This is an undergraduate's personal experience; RA posts mostly serve enrolled undergraduates in residence halls and do not cover tuition, so for you it is a gap-closer (like RA or TA work for partially funded students), not a funded route.

Opportunities in USA as a Bangladeshi doctor (BOB-MedElites live, 7 Nov 2026)
  • Two myths: that Bangladeshi doctors can only work unpaid in the USA, and that there are no scholarships for a master's. He calls both partly myth; the real gap is that students do not know the pathways (full-time job routes, visa application, funded master's) and seniors seldom guide. Internship timing: his internship ran Feb to Feb and he started applying in the November before it ended. He had felt completely lost during internship; his first research project was stuck for a year with no publication, and publications came during internship.
  • Age advantage: he says Bangladeshi doctors can start early; he is a doctor at 25, while many people finishing medical school in the US are about 30 to 32. He calls this a big advantage.
  • Pick programmes that match your own interest and experience (his are maternal health, HIV and adolescent health), not any scholarship in an unrelated field such as biological sciences; he says you would not get that scholarship.
  • IELTS: a minimum score is enough for selection, but a visa officer may look more favourably on an 8 than a 7, and English speaking plays a big role in the visa. If a visa is refused, understand the real reason. He names TOEFL or IELTS as the options.
  • Decide your destination early. Prepare for the US, UK or Australia the same way at first, but pick one. On the Middle East and Maldives route he is blunt: little career growth, and he has seen seniors come back after about 3 years to sit FCPS. He says the same effort is better spent on the US route.
  • US routes (his view): USMLE, or take a position that adds to your portfolio first, then build clinical experience and Steps; he says within three years you can get into residency. Do not wait in Bangladesh to finish everything: the earlier you enter the US system, the earlier opportunities come.
  • Research path for students in Bangladesh: start with voluntary research. Case reports in 3rd year from atypical cases, then cross-sectional, then cohort studies (prospective cohort work is the most valuable), alongside medical life. One hour a day, not eight. Build the research team: look for like-minded people; attach a professor or senior who can guide the first project; learn research methodology from first idea to manuscript (YouTube short courses, BMSS courses). Run several projects, since only one may pay off, and it takes time.
  • Avoid paid authorship: do not buy papers, pay to be listed as an author, or use anyone who charges to publish for you. He says it is very detrimental for your career, it will come out, and people see through it.
  • CV volunteering must relate to your field. A health camp does not count if you cannot relate it. His examples: research with Public Health Foundation and BMSS, work with United Nations-linked groups (as heard), community awareness (dengue, prevention), work with vulnerable groups. Then, in his words, research, research, research and research. He had 7 years of voluntary work and 3 years of research before MBBS ended.
  • Letters of recommendation matter a lot in the US. Even with a low profile, a professor who sees your potential will write a very good letter. His suggestion: one from your principal, one from the medicine department head, one from the surgery department head. He says Bangladeshis put too little effort into this.
  • Emailing professors: he emailed about 50 professors at the universities he wanted and about 30 replied wanting a Zoom meeting; some offered research positions. Email contents: who you are in one line, interest in a specific part of their work (his example was an HIV drug clinical trial), your experience, what you want to learn, then ask for a meeting date and time instead of asking if they have a position. He says a professor who is convinced makes a high scholarship easy.
  • Columbia story: the scholarship needed CGPA above 3.3, and although his MBBS marks were over 80%, he had no 3.3 CGPA. He says CGPA conversion from MBBS is of little use. He got a 50% scholarship, which he says still left about Tk 1 crore to pay, so he wrote to the professor to ask for more. MPH is a cash-in program (it needs a lot of money); Emory has the second best MPH in the US in his view, Hopkins Bloomberg the first. He did not apply to Hopkins because he had a full job.
  • Funded PhD: he says a PhD costs nothing and pays about $3,000 to $4,000 a month for a profile like his (borderline cases possible). He says direct master's or PhD applications often get rejected and that applicants who send 20 or 30 applications blindly then complain online.
  • Mindset and community: be passionate and hungry; he says he does not charge for knowledge but wants the same hunger from a mentee and does not believe in ready-made publications. He ends by urging a stronger Bangladeshi doctor community abroad, like the Indian and Pakistani ones, and says to text him if you come to the US.

Dr. Sadiqur Rahman Sadab (host) and Dr. Iftekhar Ahmed Sakib (Clinical Research Coordinator, Infectious Diseases division, Emory University School of Medicine, since March; works on HIV-immunology research). Live stream by the BOB-MedElites Facebook page, 7 Nov 2026, about 1 hr 02 min, in Bangla with English terms. Caution: One doctor's personal views and experience, not official guidance. The Bangla was machine-transcribed and noisy, so the figures from the garbled stretches (about $3,000 to $4,000 a month for a PhD, the Tk 1 crore remaining after the 50% Columbia award, the Emory and Hopkins ranking and the three-year route to residency) are his claims and were not verified.

Unanswered

Open questions that decide several routes

Each one is worth an email. The answer can open or close several routes at once.

  1. When is the MBBS conferred?

    Before or only after the internship? It decides SpaceMed, Commonwealth Shared, Maastricht and others that need the degree finished by a deadline.

  2. Maastricht admission route

    Bachelor's route (GRE needed) or bachelor's + master's route (no GRE)? Does his average convert to at least 7.5/10? Ask masteradmission-fhml@maastrichtuniversity.nl.

  3. Swedish Institute's 3,000 hours

    Paid or freelance work separate from the internship, before Feb 2027. The SI FAQ says internships don't count.

  4. Hopkins work-experience line

    The one-year line appears on the ScM page, not the PhD page. Ask BSPH.EpiAcademic@jh.edu whether the internship counts.

  5. MBBS → direct PhD in Australia and NZ

    No university says an MBBS alone qualifies. It's case by case (publications, research), with an MPhil as fallback.

  6. WES timing

    Starting in early November lands mid-December — too late for a verified 1 Dec file. Ask Hopkins and Emory if WES can follow.

  7. Hopkins work-experience line (corrected)

    The programme page lists one year of full-time related work as required, the Epi FAQ says only 'strongly recommended'; the old gate said it was on the ScM page only. Does an internship year count? Ask BSPH.EpiAcademic@jh.edu before paying $155.

  8. Does an MBBS count as the Yale bachelor's equivalent?

    Yale does not rule on MBBS and requires no master's; email phdms.publichealth@yale.edu. The PhD English rule is also Speaking-only, so ask which overall score they expect.

  9. Does an MBBS with the internship in progress meet the MRC degree rule?

    The Manchester page says First or Upper Second or international equivalent, held or about to be obtained, but does not mention MBBS. Ask fbmh.doctoralacademy.admissions@manchester.ac.uk.

  10. Emory and WES

    Laney and the programme do not require a credential evaluation, but the general Rollins how-to-apply page says international applicants must use WES. Ask Epidemiology admissions so you do not skip a required document.

  11. Can WES follow the Hopkins submission?

    Hopkins allows supporting documents within two weeks after 1 Dec, but its English waiver and completeness depend on the evaluation. Confirm what happens if WES lands after 15 Dec.

  12. Does Pittsburgh accept an MBBS and waive the fee?

    The programme expects a degree in a biological or physical science, maths, computer science or engineering, and a waiver was not found on the pages read. Ask the IBGP office.

Strong funding; ask one question about work experience first

The Johns Hopkins Bloomberg PhD in Epidemiology is a fully funded, top-ranked programme, and it's one of the few US PhDs that explicitly says a prior graduate degree isn't required. The work-experience wording is still unresolved: the programme page lists one year of full-time experience, while the FAQ says it is only strongly recommended.

Before you board

PortalSOPHAS ↗ (opens in a new tab)

SOPHAS charges $155 for the first programme and $65 for each additional one. A limited number of fee waivers exist: you must be a citizen of and currently reside in a UN Least Developed Country (Bangladesh is listed), request it before you submit, and submit within 14 days; it covers the $155 first programme only. A credential evaluation is also required: WES ICAP course-by-course at $239 (an $80 coupon is available on the waiver form for a first WES order) or ECE sent directly to Hopkins; ECFMG is not accepted. Emory does not share this fee, because its PhD runs through the Laney Graduate School, not SOPHAS.

How this was checked: Fee amounts confirmed on Liaison's SOPHAS help centre; Bloomberg's how-to-apply and international-applicant pages and the WES fee page (9 Nov 2026).

01

What it pays

  • A guaranteed minimum stipend of $52,000 a year through June 2027, plus tuition, fees and medical benefits, guaranteed for at least the first four years. The Epi FAQ adds 100% tuition for up to four years plus an NIH pre-doctoral level stipend.
  • Stipend rates beyond June 2027 depend on the union's successor agreement.
  • Cost to apply: $155 through SOPHAS for the first programme, $65 for each additional. A limited number of waivers exist (Bangladesh residents qualify; request before submitting).

02

Who can apply

  • A prior graduate degree is 'not required, but highly recommended'. GRE is not required and not reviewed.
  • Work experience: the programme page lists one year of full-time work experience in a related field, but the Epi FAQ says a year of full-time post-baccalaureate work is 'strongly recommended'. Email BSPH.EpiAcademic@jh.edu to ask whether your internship counts.
  • Three letters, from professional or academic referees or a mix; the FAQ asks for at least one academic, advisor preferred.
  • A statement of objectives and research goals, with a two-page limit per the Epi FAQ.

03

Credential evaluation and English

  • Credential evaluation is mandatory: WES ICAP course-by-course ($239, ordered through SOPHAS) or ECE sent directly to Hopkins. ECFMG is not accepted. Even if the portal lists it as optional, it is required for international coursework.
  • English minimums: IELTS Academic 7, Duolingo 130, PTE Academic 68, or TOEFL iBT 100 for scores taken before 21 Jan 2026. A TOEFL taken on the new format needs 5.0 on the 1 to 6 scale. Scores must be under two years old.
  • Waiver: only through a WES or ECE evaluation showing English was the only language of instruction for a four-year bachelor's or professional degree, and only once that evaluation is received. Medium-of-instruction letters are not accepted.

04

Dates that matter

  • 1 Dec 2026 via SOPHAS, for an August 2027 start. Submit by the deadline; supporting documents must be received within two weeks after.
  • WES takes weeks to start, so order it today.

05

How it fits the US and Europe goals

A Hopkins epidemiology PhD builds US contacts, publications and letters, and can lead to physician-scientist tracks. It also takes four to five years, so a US clinical Match lands around 2032, and an August 2027 start collides with your internship.

06

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: admission

    One of the most competitive PhDs in the field. Most successful applicants have a master's or research track record.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: work experience

    The two Hopkins pages disagree and an internship may not count.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: timing

    August 2027 starts before your internship ends.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: years since graduation

    A PhD finishing around 2031–32 means your MBBS is six years old when you apply.

07

The honest recommendation

Email the department this week, quoting both work-experience lines. If they say the internship counts and allow a later start, apply. Otherwise, next year's cycle suits your timeline better.

Emory's Rollins PhD in Epidemiology gives every admitted student full tuition and a stipend, sits next to the CDC, and shares the same 1 December deadline as Hopkins. It applies through the Laney Graduate School for $75, not SOPHAS. It's very competitive, and the same timing trade-off applies.

Before you board

PortalLaney Graduate School application (LaneyConnect), not SOPHAS ↗ (opens in a new tab)

The Laney Graduate School application fee is $75, and the Rollins how-to-apply page also states $75 for the PhD. Your notes say fee waivers exist; that was not confirmed on the pages checked. The PhD does not run through SOPHAS, so it does not share the Hopkins fee. Credential evaluation is not mandatory for Laney, but the Rollins general page says international applicants must use WES, so ask Epidemiology admissions.

How this was checked: Emory Laney requirements page, Rollins PhD Epidemiology and how-to-apply pages, 9 Nov 2026; fee waiver not confirmed.

01

What it pays

  • A full-tuition scholarship for all admitted PhD students plus a stipend of $43,260 a year (Laney, FY26–27 union rate). The Rollins programme page still says $42,000 for 2025–26, which is stale.
  • Health insurance support as part of the package.
  • Cost to apply: $75 through the Laney Graduate School application. It is separate from SOPHAS, so it does not share the Hopkins fee.

02

Who can apply

  • A bachelor's is the stated minimum, so an MBBS qualifies. GRE is optional.
  • It's very selective: more than 200 applications for 10–14 places, and admitted students often hold advanced degrees.

03

What the file needs

  • Three letters of recommendation, from people familiar with your academic performance.
  • A 500-word statement of purpose: previous research experience or training, research interests, how the programme addresses them, and long-term goals.
  • A statement on building collaborative and respectful graduate communities (500 words in the Laney application).
  • Name at least two Epidemiology graduate faculty you would like to work with.
  • Unofficial transcripts from each post-secondary institution, with a notarized translation if they are not in English. Official transcripts come only after admission.

04

Credential evaluation and English

  • Credential evaluation: the programme and Laney pages do not make it mandatory (Laney says international applicants 'may want to consider' it). But the Rollins general how-to-apply page says international applicants must use WES, and that page covers all degrees. Ask Epidemiology admissions before you decide.
  • English: TOEFL or IELTS for international applicants. No numeric minimum for Epidemiology was found on the official pages, so ask the programme.

05

Dates that matter

  • 1 Dec 2026 is the final deadline for PhD applicants; Emory deadlines fall at midnight US Eastern.
  • Shortlisted applicants get a virtual visit day, most often a Friday in the first two weeks of February.

06

How it fits the US and Europe goals

An Emory PhD gives you CDC-adjacent networks and US letters. It's also several years on F-1 status before any Match, and your MBBS year of graduation ages meanwhile.

07

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: admission

    The competition is heavy for a first-time researcher.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: timing

    An August 2027 start doesn't fit the internship.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: clinical gap

    Five years without patient care.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: credential evaluation unclear

    The pages disagree on whether WES is needed, so ask early to avoid a surprise.

08

The honest recommendation

Apply only if you're committed to the research route and have an answer on start dates; this is a separate Laney application. If the 2029 Match is the priority, the paid US research job route is better.

PortalSOPHAS, via the Emory Rollins admissions FAQ ↗ (opens in a new tab)

The 5 Jan 2027 priority deadline means the application must be complete AND verified by SOPHAS by then; verification can take up to 10 business days, so submit in mid-December. Emory urges international applicants to submit by 1 May 2027 at the latest. The $75 Emory fee on its pages is for the PhD, not this MPH.

01

What it pays

  • Merit awards of 50-100% of tuition; all full-time MPH students, internationals included, whose applications are complete and verified in SOPHAS by 5 Jan are automatically considered. Awards include a REAL award and a practicum award; the notes' practicum figures were not re-confirmed.
  • Rollins Earn and Learn (REAL): work and earn up to $3,000 per semester (fall and spring only), first come first served. International students who are eligible to work apply after they are admitted; Emory and Emory Healthcare employees are not eligible.
  • Estimated total cost of attendance for 2026-27 is $85,356 (tuition $43,264, i.e. $21,632 a semester), so partial awards still leave a large bill. The Financial Aid PDF is stale (it shows $82,514 for 2025-26); use the Rollins page.

Before you board

PortalNo single portal: USAJobs for federal posts, university career pages for the rest ↗ (opens in a new tab)

There is no application fee for searching or applying to these posts. Posts are advertised employer by employer (USAJobs for federal posts, university and hospital career pages, NIH institute pages). Costs start only at the visa stage: if ECFMG sponsors your J-1, that is a $370 annual fee, $220 SEVIS and the J-1 visa fee (see the ECFMG J-1 card).

How this was checked: Checked 3 Nov 2026 against ECFMG's EVSP fees page for the sponsorship leg; the route itself has no central portal or fee, so nothing more could be verified.

01

What it pays

  • Each post sets its own salary. No official figure exists for the route as a whole. The board's Mayo example is about $67-79k a year.
  • No application fee. If ECFMG sponsors your J-1, the sponsorship costs are $370 (annual) + $220 SEVIS + the J-1 visa fee.
  • ECFMG-sponsored scholars must be funded at $1,600 a month or more.

02

Who can apply

  • Anyone with a conferred MBBS whom a host lab will take. Whether USMLE is needed depends on the host and was not confirmed.
  • Avoid unpaid posts. The route only works if the host pays you and sponsors the visa.

03

Dates that matter

  • Rolling all year. Posts open and close on their own dates.
  • The board's advice is to start emailing principal investigators in May-July 2027 for a post-internship start.
  • Allow time after an offer for the DS-2019 and the visa interview in Dhaka; processing times were not verified.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

For the 2029 Match this is the most useful thing you can do with 2027-28: US letters of recommendation, recent graduation and a salary that protects your $30,000. For Europe it only helps indirectly, as a stronger CV for a later funded MPH or PhD. It does not count towards any European licence.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: no central route

    You find each post yourself. Mass emails get ignored, so each one must show you have read the lab's papers.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: no publications yet

    You are competing with people who have papers. Any thesis, audit or case report from the internship helps.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: visa rules are unsettled

    The board's own tracking says the H-1B $100,000 fee is tied up in court and that university guidance (7 Oct, still current at the board's 1 Nov check) said it was not being collected; none of this is confirmed on the official fee pages, so treat it as unsettled. Cap-exempt university employers avoid the cap-subject fee issues, and J-1 via ECFMG is the safer leg.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: research is not clinical experience

    You will have little or no patient contact, and the time does not count as residency training. The two-year home rule may apply to a J-1 if US or Bangladeshi government funding is involved.

06

The honest recommendation

Make this your main plan for 2027-28. Use the internship year to build a CV, pick 20 to 30 labs in epidemiology and public health, and start writing in May-July 2027. Insist on a paid post and ask the host early which visa they use.

  • The board's current MD-eligible examples: Immunology (Oh lab, Scottsdale, ID 390313) and Dermatology (Wyles lab, Rochester, ID 393086, where MDs need substantial research and publications).
  • A Jacksonville Neuroscience post (ID 393271) wants a computational PhD, so it is not for you.

03

Dates that matter

  • No deadline. Immunology was posted 1 Sep 2026 and Dermatology 9 Oct 2026.
  • Job alerts on the portal are the practical tool. Start applying after the MBBS is conferred, aiming at a post-internship start.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

A year at Mayo gives you the US letters, US research and recent-graduate status the Match rewards, while paying you. For Europe it is a prestige line on an MPH or PhD application, nothing more. It does not lead to a European licence.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: no publications

    Posts that take MDs often expect real research output. Your thesis and any internship project are your evidence.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: posts disappear in days

    Check weekly and apply the moment you are eligible.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: not clinical work

    You will not see patients, and this does not replace US clinical experience.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: visa depends on the department

    Ask early whether the department sponsors a visa and which type; the ECFMG J-1 leg is covered on its own card.

06

The honest recommendation

Treat Mayo as one target among many. Set job alerts now so you learn what fits, then apply widely to labs at other universities too. Do not wait on Mayo alone.

01

What it costs

  • $370 ECFMG annual application fee (every year of sponsorship), $220 SEVIS, and the J-1 visa fee, listed as $160 on ECFMG's page.
  • Special appeals, only if needed: $367 (State Department) + $200 (ECFMG).
  • Minimum funding for the exchange visitor is $1,600 a month. ECFMG does not pay you; the host does.

02

Who can apply

  • You, with a US host that has offered a research post and is working with ECFMG. Your host's Training Program Liaison coordinates the application, and you apply through MyIntealth.
  • The board's card says USMLE and ECFMG certification are generally not required for this category; confirm with ECFMG.

03

Dates that matter

  • Rolling, tied to the start date of the appointment. The $370 fee is annual.
  • Nothing to do until you hold an offer, which opens only after the MBBS is conferred.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

This is plumbing for the paid-research-post route, and it is the safest visa leg when the host cannot sponsor directly. It matters only for the US goal. A year on a J-1 research scholar visa builds the letters and research the Match looks for, but it does not count as clinical experience.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: no offer, no sponsorship

    ECFMG does not find you a job.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: no patient care

    The board describes the category as research with no or incidental patient contact, so check what your host plans.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: the two-year home rule

    It may apply if US or Bangladeshi government funding is involved. Ask your host before accepting.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: fees recur and move

    The $370 repeats each year and the visa fee line should be re-checked before you pay.

06

The honest recommendation

Do not spend time here yet. Read the EVSP checklist once so nothing surprises you, then put the effort into getting offers. Budget about $750 for year one and ask each host whether they sponsor directly or through ECFMG.

Since 12 Jan 2026 international graduates register and pay for the Step exams through FSMB (usmle.fsmb.org); ECFMG still decides eligibility. 01

What it costs

  • ECFMG certification application $580. Step 1 $905 ($695 + $210 surcharge). Step 2 CK $930 ($695 + $235). Pathway application $945.
  • That is $3,360 in listed fees. OET Medicine, prep material, ERAS and the Match come on top.
  • All amounts are USD. Fees change each year and the April 2026 schedule applies to 2027.

02

Who can apply

  • Graduates of schools listed in WDOMS with an ECFMG sponsor note. Check your school's note on wdoms.org before paying for anything.
  • Register through FSMB for the exams and MyIntealth for certification.

03

Dates that matter

  • Exams run all year in three-month eligibility periods, so there is no single exam deadline.
  • 2027 Pathways close 31 Jan 2027; the 2028 season is not announced.
  • The 2027 Match is too early for you. Target 2028 or 2029. Step 2 CK is the score screen.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

Everything in the US plan runs through this. For Europe it does nothing for licensing, though a strong Step 2 CK score still signals ability in an MPH or PhD application. With no licence, the board reads Pathway 6 (Mini-CEX) as the realistic clinical-skills option.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: sponsor note

    If your school's WDOMS sponsor note does not cover your graduation year, check with ECFMG before you pay.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: new exam format

    The board notes Step 1 and Step 2 CK now use 30-minute blocks. Practise with the new tutorial.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: the stack grows

    Add OET, a prep resource, a clinical placement and the Match. Keep a running budget.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: rules move

    The board is tracking visa and J-1 policy changes. Re-read ECFMG news before each payment.

06

The honest recommendation

Start Step 1 preparation during the internship, since it is the one step entirely in your hands. Do not pay the Pathway fee until the 2028 season opens and you know which Match year you are targeting.

Before you board

PortalNo central portal: contact NIH labs directly (OITE: training.nih.gov) ↗ (opens in a new tab)

NIH's official pages state no application fee, and there is no central application to pay for. Approaching principal investigators and registering with OITE are free. Once a lab selects you, NIH's Division of International Services processes the Visiting Program case and NIH sponsors the J-1 itself, not ECFMG. Government visa fees apply later.

How this was checked: Checked 3 Nov 2026 against NIMH and NIAID training pages and NIH Division of International Services guidance; no fee stated, none found.

01

What it pays

  • A stipend scaled by experience. No official figure was verified.
  • No application fee stated. NIH sponsors your J-1; visa-stage government fees would apply.

02

Who can apply

  • A Visiting Fellow holds a doctoral degree with under five years of relevant postdoctoral experience. The board cites NIH policy as "PhD, MD or equivalent".
  • Whether your MBBS counts as MD-equivalent is not confirmed. Ask NIH's Division of International Services (DIS) before investing time.

03

Dates that matter

  • No deadline. Labs fill posts when they have an opening.
  • You cannot start before your MBBS is conferred, so think 2027-28.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

If it works, it is among the best CV lines for a US residency application: recent US research, an NIH letter and a paid year. It does nothing for a European licence. It is also open-ended, with the whole process decided by one lab's budget.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: eligibility is unconfirmed

    If NIH does not treat the MBBS as a doctoral degree, the route is closed.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: you do not apply to NIH centrally

    You apply to labs, and the lab chooses.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: no track record

    Fellows usually bring research experience; you have none yet.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: not clinical

    It does not count as US clinical experience.

06

The honest recommendation

Send one short email to DIS asking whether an MBBS qualifies. If yes, add NIH labs to the same outreach list as your other US posts. If no, you have lost nothing.
