Before you board

PortalSOPHAS (most schools of public health); some use their own portal ↗ (opens in a new tab)

SOPHAS charges $155 for the first programme and $65 for each additional one. Some programmes add their own fee. Bangladesh is on SOPHAS's Least Developed Countries list, so you can request the international fee waiver, which covers the $155 first fee only; apply before you submit. Some schools, such as UNC Gillings' PhD, use their own portal.

How this was checked: Checked 3 Nov 2026 against the SOPHAS Fees and Fee Waivers page on Liaison's Applicant Help Center.

01

What it pays

  • The funding comes from each university's own offer (tuition waiver plus stipend), not from SOPHAS. Terms differ per school, so read the offer.
  • Application fee: $155 first programme, $65 each extra. Bangladesh is on SOPHAS's Least Developed Countries list, so you can request the international fee waiver (limited and first-come; it covers the first $155 only, so apply before you submit).

02

Who can apply

  • An MBBS is usually accepted for direct entry. JHU Epidemiology needs TOEFL 100 (5.0 on the new TOEFL scale) or IELTS 7 and does not review the GRE. Harvard PHS requires the GRE.
  • UNC does not need the GRE; funding there is not guaranteed and files incomplete on 31 Jan are not reviewed.

03

Dates that matter

  • 1 Dec 2026 for JHU and Harvard (Harvard 5 pm). 15 Dec 2026 for UNC. JHU's PhD in Clinical Investigation closes 1 Mar 2027.
  • No single deadline: each programme page is the authority.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

A PhD is a research-career route, not a faster way to residency. Four to six years of non-clinical work leaves you seven to nine years past graduation at Match time. It can bring a visa, US mentors and strong letters, but you cannot do it and the 2029 Match together.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: timing

    You would need test scores, three letters and a research statement within weeks.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: no research record

    Admissions committees expect evidence of research ability.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: Match conflict

    The PhD runs into the 2030s and weakens a clinical application.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: funding terms vary

    Department funding is not always guaranteed.

06

The honest recommendation

Apply only if you have genuinely decided that research matters more than the 2029 Match. If that is you, prepare JHU first, since it needs no GRE, and use the Bangladesh fee waiver. If the Match is the priority, skip it.

The Sakib model is a personal route, not a funder: a US MPH applied for through SOPHAS with partial money, then on-campus and later paid research work. Before you board

PortalSOPHAS help centre: fee waiver page (MPH programmes apply via SOPHAS; US research jobs have no central portal) ↗ (opens in a new tab)

SOPHAS charges $155 for the first programme and $65 for each extra one, and some programmes add a supplemental fee (e.g. UIC $80). Bangladesh is on the UN Least Developed Countries list, so a citizen who lives there can request a fee waiver in the application: request it BEFORE you submit, you must submit within 14 days of approval (no extension), and it covers only the first $155. The same form offers an $80 coupon off the WES evaluation (first order only). Processing takes up to 10 business days; call 617-612-2090 to check that waiver funds are left. Job applications carry no standard fee.

How this was checked: SOPHAS fees and waiver page re-read on 9 Nov 2026; F-1 rules checked on the DHS Study in the States pages.

01

What it pays and costs

  • SOPHAS: $155 first programme, $65 each extra, and some programmes add a supplemental fee.
  • Fee waiver: as a citizen who currently lives in a UN Least Developed Country (Bangladesh is on the list) you can request one inside the application. It covers only the first $155, is first come first served, and funds can run out, so phone SOPHAS (617-612-2090) first.
  • The same form lets you request an $80 coupon off the WES evaluation (first order only; the course-by-course ICAP costs $239).
  • MPH money is decided school by school and is partial, so the gap is covered by on-campus work and later jobs.

02

Who can apply

  • Anyone applying to a SOPHAS programme. Each school sets its own requirements.
  • Applying while your MBBS or internship is still running is normal: you can submit before transcripts and letters arrive, and offers are contingent on a final transcript proving the degree is complete before you enrol.
  • The model is a personal account relayed on the board, not an official source.

03

Dates that matter

  • The 2026-27 SOPHAS cycle opened 12 Aug 2026 and closes 2 Aug 2027, but each programme sets an earlier deadline.
  • Waiver clock: once approved, you must submit within 14 days, including weekends and holidays; processing takes up to 10 business days, so request it only when the file is nearly ready.
  • Examples: Brown and Columbia 1 Dec 2026; Emory 5 Jan; Georgia State 15 Feb 2027.

04

The F-1 work rules

  • On campus: at most 20 hours a week while school is in session; assistantships count as on-campus work.
  • CPT: only after one full academic year of full-time study and it must be part of the curriculum; a year of full-time CPT removes OPT eligibility.
  • OPT: 12 months of work authorisation after each higher level of study (24 more for STEM-eligible degrees).

05

How it fits the US and Europe goals

Classes starting mid-2027 clash with an internship that runs to about late 2027, so most realistic starts are 2028. A one-year MPH then ends around mid-2029, after the September 2028 ERAS window, which makes 2029 hard and 2030 more likely. It still builds Step 1 time, US research jobs and letters.

For Europe it supports public health or research roles, not clinical licensing.

06

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: funding is not guaranteed

    Assistantships and scholarships vary by programme and are partial.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: timing

    The internship overlaps the 2027 intake and the degree pushes the Match later.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: US cost of living

    Tuition gaps and living costs can use up $30,000 fast, and first-year funds must be documented for the I-20 regardless of future earnings.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: F-1 work limits

    No off-campus work in year one.

07

The honest recommendation

It is one of the few routes here you largely control. Apply to a short list of MPH programmes with the fee waiver requested for the first one, and decide the start year only after seeing which offers come with real money.

What it pays

How it fits the US and Europe goals

A funded MPH could add a research record and a network, but it does not replace Step 1, Step 2 CK or ECFMG certification. Because half the award is a loan, a US master's would still cost far more than your budget, and the UK is excluded.

  1. 01

Yale's PhD in Public Health guarantees every admitted student five years of tuition and stipend, and the epidemiology concentrations do not accept the GRE. The five-year acceptance rate is 3%, the average admitted GPA is 3.8, and the deadline is 1 Dec 2026, 11:59 pm Eastern through the GSAS portal, not SOPHAS.

Before you board

PortalYale GSAS PhD/Master's application (not SOPHAS) ↗ (opens in a new tab)

The fee is $105 for all degree-seeking applicants. US citizens, permanent residents and non-US citizens can all request a fee waiver. Yale's PhD in Public Health does not use SOPHAS (that is for the Yale MPH). Letters do not have to arrive before you submit, but programmes begin reviewing soon after the deadline.

How this was checked: Yale GSAS fee and deadline pages and the YSPH PhD page, 9 Nov 2026.

01

What it pays

  • Five years guaranteed for all YSPH PhD students: tuition ($52,400 in 2026-27) plus a 12-month stipend, from fellowships, teaching fellowships, traineeships and research assistantships.
  • GSAS minimum stipends for 2026-27 are $52,046 (humanities, social and physical sciences) and $53,629 (biological and biomedical). Which band Public Health falls in is not stated.
  • A one-time $1,500 relocation award, and a health award covering single-student Yale Health coverage. The YSPH FAQ adds spouse and family coverage and a subsidy for children under 18.
  • Cost to apply: $105, and non-US citizens can request a waiver.

02

Who can apply

  • A master's is not required; a bachelor's or international equivalent can apply, even while still in progress if it is awarded before matriculation. Some programmes prefer post-baccalaureate training.
  • Whether a Bangladeshi MBBS counts is not ruled on. Email phdms.publichealth@yale.edu.
  • GRE: required only for Biostatistics and Health Policy and Management. It is not accepted for Chronic Disease Epidemiology, Environmental Health Sciences, Epidemiology of Microbial Diseases or Social and Behavioral Sciences.
  • English: TOEFL iBT or IELTS Academic only, no Duolingo. See the catches for the Speaking minimums.

03

Dates that matter

  • 1 Dec 2026, 11:59 pm Eastern, which is late morning on 2 Dec in Dhaka. Deadlines are subject to change at any time.
  • The Fall 2027 application is open at apply.grad.yale.edu/apply.
  • Decisions mostly Feb to early March; reply by 15 April.

04

What the file needs

  • 3 letters of recommendation, entered by name in the application, uploaded by recommenders via link.
  • A CV. A writing sample is not required.
  • A statement of research interests and faculty fit; you can list up to three faculty and need no mentor in advance. The page states no word limit.
  • Unofficial transcripts are enough to apply, in English or translated. No credential evaluation requirement was seen, though no explicit 'no WES' statement was found.

05

How it fits the US and Europe goals

A Yale public health PhD would give strong US letters and a research record, but it takes about five years on F-1 status before any residency application. The 2029 Match plan (Step 1, paid US research job, Step 2 CK) is the faster clinical route.

06

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: odds

    The five-year average acceptance rate is 3%, the average admitted GPA is 3.8, and there is no minimum GPA.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: English Speaking minimum

    The PhD page asks for minimum Speaking scores to teach: TOEFL 26+ for tests before 21 Jan 2026, or 5.5+ on the new scale; IELTS 8.0 or higher as written. Admitted PhD averages are TOEFL 106 and IELTS 7.5. TOEFL 100 and IELTS 7.0 are the MS rule, not the PhD rule.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: English waiver

    Exempt only if your undergraduate degree is from a school where English is the primary language of instruction and you studied in residence at least three years. An advanced degree does not count. Ask whether your MBBS qualifies.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: one concentration

    The notes say only one GSAS application is allowed per year and PhD non-admits are not reconsidered for the MS; this was not re-checked on the official page.

07

The honest recommendation

A very long shot. If you are committed to the research route, apply to Chronic Disease Epidemiology or Epidemiology of Microbial Diseases, email phdms.publichealth@yale.edu about MBBS equivalence now, and book an English test with a strong Speaking score. If the 2029 Match is the priority, do not let this crowd out Step 1.
